Roneat是高棉語對柬埔寨傳統木琴與金屬琴的統稱，屬體鳴樂器。其音條以竹、硬木: Roneat is the Khmer term for the xylophones and metallophones of Cambodia, which are idiophones. Their bars are made of bamboo, hardwood or metal and are set on a long or boat-shaped frame, and they are struck with two beaters; they are common in pinpeat and mohaori ensembles and also appear in Khmer classical music.

站於琴前，雙手持棒敲擊琴鍵中央。手持樂器本體，透過敲擊、搖晃、刮奏或撥彈等方式使: Stand in front of the instrument and strike the middle of the bars with a beater in each hand. The instrument itself is held in the hand and made to vibrate by striking, shaking, scraping or plucking, so that its own body sounds. Different parts and different amounts of force give different timbres. When practising, first check that the way you hold the instrument is right, then learn the basic way of making it sound, and only after that work on rhythm patterns and melody. Fingers or beaters strike a surface and rebound naturally off it, with the wrist relaxed.

羅乃木琴為柬埔寨體鳴樂器，發聲條依類型而異：roneat thmor 以石條發聲: The roneat is a Cambodian idiophone, and what sounds differs by type: roneat thmor sounds with stone bars; the ordinary roneat may use bamboo bars, other good-quality wooden bars or metal bars. The roneat ek has twenty-one thick bamboo or hardwood bars hung by cord on both sides of a boat-shaped resonator; the roneat thung is also boat-shaped, but its material is not given. The roneat dek is built from twenty-one bars of black iron. The source does not state the particular wood, or the decorative materials, of the frame and resonator.
羅乃木琴用於柬埔寨傳統音樂與古典音樂，常見於皮帕特（pinpeat）與莫哈瑞（m: The roneat is used in Cambodian traditional and classical music and is common in the pinpeat and mohaori (also mahori) ensembles. In the pinpeat ensemble the roneat ek sits to the right of the lower-pitched roneat thung; the roneat thung belonged to the pinpeat already before the Angkor period; the roneat dek can also be used in pinpeat and mohaori. Post-Angkorian murals often show them in these two kinds of traditional ensemble.
羅乃木琴音色明亮清脆，具有典型的木質溫潤特徵。其音域寬廣，從中音至高音範圍均有涵: The roneat has a bright, clear timbre, with the warm character typical of wood. Its range is wide, covering everything from the middle to the top register, and the different types of roneat each have their own range. The resonance produced when the wooden bars are struck carries well, and the tone loses neither its warmth nor a certain metallic quality. Compared with other Southeast Asian xylophones such as the Thai ranat, the roneat sounds a little softer and has a distinctive Eastern character. Its resonance depends mainly on the resonator tubes below the frame, which lengthen each note effectively. All in all the roneat has a carrying, expressive tone, and it plays the leading melodic role in Cambodian traditional ensembles.
自扶南起，音樂已用於寺廟、節慶與皇家儀式，Roneat（羅乃木琴）被認為早於吳哥: From Funan onward, music was used in temples, festivals and royal ritual, and the roneat is thought to have existed before the Angkor period; the roneat thung was already a member of the pinpeat ensemble before Angkor. Stone xylophones have been seen in Cambodia and in the central highlands of Vietnam, the latter about 2,500 years old. Recent hidden murals at Angkor Wat show a traditional ensemble including a roneat, perhaps the earliest image of one. Its types derive from the Javanese gamelan and spread north-west to Myanmar; when Jayavarman II returned from Java in 802 and founded his kingdom, and through the post-Angkorian period, murals often show the roneat ek and roneat thung in pinpeat and mohaori ensembles.
